> `obs_count` is **not comparable across runs** — most fetchers report rows merged this run, thirteen fall back to the whole store when nothing was written. To ask how big this source is, count the store. See ledger R326 and the comment in `updater/state.py`.

> A `partial` NEVER sets `last_success_utc` (R231). A source reading `last SUCCESS: NEVER` may be ingesting millions of rows perfectly well and failing one sub-unit. Check `obs_count` and the run history before concluding it is dead.

> **A FUTURE `last_obs_date` IS USUALLY CORRECT, NOT A BUG.** Many publishers ship genuine PROJECTIONS: CSO Ireland's `18_Population_Projections` runs to 2057, Estonia's `rahvastik` to 2085, ABS to 2046/2071, UN WPP to 2101, IMF WEO to 2031. `health.py` already separates the two — `frontier` is the furthest period held INCLUDING projections (display only), `newest_obs` filters to periods <= today and is the recency signal — because 28 of 93 units legitimately reported a future frontier. Do NOT "repair" a future date until you have looked at the series key and the year sequence.
>
> What IS a defect: a SENTINEL (9999-12-31, 2999-12-31) or a COUNTER read as a year (years 1, 2, 3 ... contiguous from 1 — no projection starts at year 1). Tell them apart by the key and the sequence, never by the size of the number. See R320/R322 and `tools/audit_impossible_dates.py`, whose bounds (before 1500, after 2200) are deliberately far outside every real projection horizon.

## 3. How it works

**Why this strategy** (registry `strategy_reason`):

> PxWeb source: tables expose an 'updated' timestamp and accept selection queries, so detect changed tables via 'updated' and re-POST only recent time-dim values, upserting per database — the PxWeb analogue of updatedAfter/startPeriod.

**Adapter contract** (registry `adapter`):

- `vintage_signal`: PxWeb per-table metadata 'updated' field (GET table metadata at https://px.hagstofa.is/pxis/api/v1/...): compare each table's 'updated' to last ingest, re-pull only changed tables.
- `since_param`: PxWeb selection 'values' filter on the time dimension (post only the latest period codes, i.e. period >= last_obs+1); no literal startPeriod query string — selection is a POSTed JSON query.
- `out_paths_note`: per-database files data/clean_full/hagstofa/{Efnahagur,Atvinnuvegir,Ibuar,Samfelag,Umhverfi}.parquet (5 files) plus _catalog.json.
- `rate_note`: No key; RATE=0.3s between calls, 429 → sleep 30s; MAX_CELLS=100000 caps large tables (silently aggregates non-time dims — coverage limit, not a refresh blocker).

**Fetcher module**: [`updater/strategies/fetchers/hagstofa.py`](../../updater/strategies/fetchers/hagstofa.py)

<details><summary>Its own module docstring — the authoritative description, including every defect previously found and why the code looks the way it does</summary>

```
S3 (sdmx_delta) fetcher — Statistics Iceland (Hagstofa Íslands), PxWeb. No key.

License: CC BY 4.0.  Source: https://px.hagstofa.is/pxen/api/v1/en (PxWeb v1, JSON-stat2).

LAYOUT (set by jobs/ingest_hagstofa.py): ONE parquet per DATABASE under
clean_full/hagstofa/<db>.parquet (db in Atvinnuvegir / Efnahagur / Ibuar /
Samfelag / Umhverfi). Schema is (series_key, obs_date, value):
  series_key : "ICE:<db>:<path-with-/-as-:>:<dim>=<code>[:<dim>=<code>...]" where the
               leading "ICE:<db>:<path>" segment (through the ".px" leaf) identifies
               the source TABLE and the trailing "<dim>=<code>" tokens identify the
               non-time cell within that table. This is exactly what parse_jsonstat2
               (reused verbatim from the ingester) emits, so re-fetched rows collide
               with their on-disk twins and merge dedup overwrites revisions in place.
  obs_date   : date32, parsed from the PxWeb time dimension code (parse_date).
  value      : float64.
DEDUP KEY = (series_key, obs_date) — the exact key the ingester wrote.

SUB-UNIT = one PxWeb TABLE (a catalog entry). The catalog (data/clean_full/hagstofa/
_catalog.json) — written by the ingester's crawl — is REUSED verbatim (db / path / id),
never re-discovered. There are ~1900 tables across 5 databases.

DATE-TAIL (cheap incremental): for each table we read its on-disk max(obs_date)
(from the rows whose series_key starts with that table's prefix), GET the live PxWeb
metadata to find the time variable + its sorted time codes, and POST a query that
restricts the time dimension to ONLY the codes whose parsed date is >= the stored
max (boundary INCLUSIVE so an in-place revision of the latest period is captured;
merge dedups the overlap). Non-time dimensions are selected exactly as the ingester
did (all values when the full cube fits MAX_CELLS, else the aggregate/first slice).
A table with NO on-disk history is fetched in FULL (all time codes) — a first landing.

HONEST STATUS (Tally + finalize):
  Per table we record:
    added_unit(n)    rows successfully parsed (n>0 new, n==0 net-empty-but-flowed)
    empty_unit()     a legitimately quiet tail (no time codes newer than the boundary)
                     or a table the catalog lists but PxWeb now 404/400s with no history
    transient_unit() timeout / 5xx / 429 / network drop / non-JSON 200 -> KEEP GOING
    structural_unit() a 200 with a real metadata envelope (variables present) but the
                     time dimension is gone, OR a FULL (no-date-filter) fetch of a
                     table that HAS on-disk history parsed 0 rows from a real body
  finalize() then returns 'ok'/'no_change' only when nothing transient/structural-
  failed; 'partial' on any transient (orchestrator does NOT stamp success -> re-run);
  DefinitiveError on a structural break or a large all-empty window. Existing data is
  ALWAYS preserved — every write goes through merge.merge_and_write (never-shrink).

ONE entry point: update(unit, since) -> Result. detect_change is the strategy's job.
```

</details>

**Ingest script(s)**: `jobs/ingest_hagstofa.py`

## 4. If it stops updating — diagnose in this order

Run everything from `E:\research\econfindatalibrary`.

```bash
# 1. What does the system actually say? (not what you remember)
python -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config;con=sqlite3.connect(f'file:{config.STATE_DB}?mode=ro',uri=True);print(*con.execute(\"SELECT unit_id,status,last_success_utc,last_attempt_utc,last_error FROM unit_state WHERE source_id='hagstofa'\"),sep=chr(10))"

# 2. Is it even being ATTEMPTED? 'scheduled' is not 'attempted' (R246).
#    A daily run reaches ~20 of ~106 cloud sources; most are skipped on cadence, which is normal.
python -m updater.run --source hagstofa --dry

# 3. Run it for real and READ THE REASON. Failures name themselves now.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -u -m updater.run --source hagstofa --force

# 4. Is the PUBLISHER healthy, or is it us? Probe upstream directly, never a relay.
#    (DBnomics is BANNED — every source must be reached at its own publisher.)

# 5. Is the store intact? obs_count in state is NOT the answer.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config,blob;d=config.source_dir('hagstofa');fs=[f for f in blob.list_parquets(d) if not os.path.basename(f).startswith('_')];print(len(fs),'files',sum(blob.row_count(os.path.join(d,os.path.basename(f))) for f in fs),'rows')"

# 6. Are its dates real? A counter-as-year or a 9999 sentinel is silent (7 sources hit).
#    NOTE: a FUTURE date is usually a legitimate projection - check the key before repairing.
python tools/audit_impossible_dates.py --r2 --source hagstofa
```

**Read the failure class before fixing anything.** From the 2026-08-04 audit of every unfetchable source, the causes were: `budget_deferral` (NOT broken — ran out of its time slice), `code_bug`, `rate_limited`, `gated_by_design`. **Zero** were an expired credential or a dead endpoint, although that is the usual first guess.

If the error names sub-units as `deferred (budget N min)` or `budget spent`, **nothing has failed** — the source ran out of its slice and the rest is taken next tick (R303). Do not 'fix' it.

## 4b. Root cause when this was last investigated (2026-08-04)

*From the unfetchable-source audit — 29 agents, every finding challenged by a skeptic before it was accepted. This source was covered by the target `hagstofa`.*

- **root cause**: `code_bug`  (confidence high)
- **blast radius**: 2 of 1074 attempted sub-units this run (0.19%). ZERO rows lost or corrupted: merge is never-shrink and both tables' history is intact on disk (UMH11120 16,199 rows / 240 series keys, UMH11165 1,795 rows / 24 keys, both spanning 1949-12-31..2024-12-31). Zero rows missed either - upstream `updated` is 2024-09-06 and the latest real year is 2024, which is already stored, so the correct parse would have merged 128 + 16 revision rows that dedup to nothing new. The real damage is source-level, not table-level: 2 false "structural" verdicts make _common.finalize() raise DefinitiveError, so all ~1074 tables' work is reported as a schema break and hagstofa has stamped `partial` with a structural-break error on every run since at least 2026-07-14 (6 consecutive runs in the runs table), never a clean success, and the series_cursors computed in that run are thrown away with the exception. Wider class: the identical "resolve the axis from full metadata, then pass only the time:true flag into the parser on a truncated response" pattern exists in scb.py:619-620, ssb.py:384/624, stat_estonia.py:608-609, stat_slovenia.py:722-723, statfin.py:578-579 - read, not probed, so unverified for those publishers.
- fixable by us: **True**

**Recommended fix, in order:**

> One line, in updater/strategies/fetchers/hagstofa.py:378-379: stop discarding the axis already resolved at line 356. Replace `rows = parse_jsonstat2(resp, prefix, meta_time_code)` with `rows = parse_jsonstat2(resp, prefix, (tvar or {}).get("code") or meta_time_code)`. `_time_var` resolves against the FULL metadata value list (date_parse_rate 0.938 on 'Ar'), which is strictly better-informed than the date-tail-truncated axis in the response (0.167). Verified on the live bodies: this yields 128 rows for UMH11120 and 16 for UMH11165 with series_keys byte-identical to what is already on disk, so no key churn and merge dedups cleanly. Second, harden core/pxweb.resolve_time_dim's step-3 last resort (core/pxweb.py:216-219): it currently returns the first TIME_CODES name in dimension order, which is how a month axis outranks a year axis - it should prefer the highest-parse-rate named candidate (even below min_rate) over dimension order, i.e. 'Ar' at 0.167 beats 'Manudur' at 0.000. Third (cheap, optional): in `_newer_time_codes`, keeping unparseable codes is right for genuine unknown periods but here it retains PxWeb normal-period sentinels ('3000'-'3005' = "Average 1951-1980" etc.) that dominate the truncated axis; nothing breaks if they stay, once the fix above lands. Fourth, sweep the same discard pattern in scb/ssb/stat_estonia/stat_slovenia/statfin (file:lines above) - one reported example is one instance of a class. Fifth, unrelated but measured: the budget `break` in hagstofa.update() should call tally.deferred_unit() for the untouched tables so the ~832 deferred ones are visible per R303 instead of silent.

<details><summary>Evidence produced during that investigation — HTTP codes, file:line, measured counts. Re-verify before acting: it was true on 2026-08-04.</summary>

Variables: 'Maelistoed'(10), 'Manudur'(12), 'Ar'(81), 'Eining'(2). CRITICAL: NO variable carries `time: true` (meta_time_code resolves to None). Same for UMH11165.px (HTTP 200, 1660 bytes, vars 'Manudur'(12), 'Ar'(81), 'Stadur'(2), no time flag).

Same for UMH11165.px -> HTTP 200, 1926 bytes, `"updated":"2024-09-06T11:00:00Z"`, value len 144, 136 non-null. NOTHING UPSTREAM CHANGED - these are ordinary JSON-stat2 cubes.
- The response's `role` object is EMPTY (`"role":{}` -> core.pxweb.role_time_of() = None) on both offenders, so the parser has no authoritative time axis at all.
- THE DEFECT, measured: our own date-tail selection starves our own resolver. The full 'Ar' axis in the metadata has 81 codes and date_parse_rate = 0.938. The date-tail restricts it to ['2024','3001','3002','3003','3004','3005'] (UMH11120) / ['2024','3004','3003','3002','3001','3000'] (UMH11165) - one real year plus 5 PxWeb normal-period SENTINELS whose labels are 'Average precipitation 1951-1980', 'Average 1961-1990', etc. On the truncated axis date_parse_rate collapses to 0.167, BELOW core/pxweb.py:182 min_rate=0.6, so the value-driven branch (core/pxweb.py:210 `if rate < min_rate: continue`) rejects every dimension.
- Falling through to core/pxweb.py step 3 (literal-name last resort) returns the FIRST TIME_CODES name in dimension order, which is 'Manudur' (month, codes '0'..'11') - printed by my instrumented run: `-> resolve_time_dim = 1 (Manudur)` for UMH11120 and `-> resolve_time_dim = 0 (Manudur)` for UMH11165. Month codes parse to no date, and the label fallback ('January','February',...) parses to no date either, so every one of the 1077 / 136 non-null observations is skipped -> parse_jsonstat2 returns 0 rows. This is exactly the name-first defect core/pxweb.py's own docstring says it exists to kill, resurfacing through its last-resort branch.
- COUNTERFACTUAL on the same 200 body: parse_jsonstat2(resp, prefix, time_code='Ar') -> 128 rows for UMH11120 and 16 rows for UMH11165, and the keys it emits are byte-identical to what is already on disk: forced sample key 'ICE:Umhverfi:1_natturufar:2_vedurfar:UMH11120.px:Maelistoed=0:Manudur=0:Eining=0' == the on-disk key in data/clean_full/hagstofa/Umhverfi.parquet. So the parser can read the body perfectly; it is only being handed the wrong axis.
- SECOND COUNTERFACTUAL (same table, no date filter): POST UMH11165.px with the FULL 81-code 'Ar' axis -> HTTP 200, 13166 bytes, date_parse_rate 0.938, `resolve_time_dim = 1 (Ar)`, parse_jsonstat2 -> 1795 rows. That is EXACTLY the 1795 rows already stored for that prefix on disk. The table parses fine at full width and only fails when we narrow it.
- CONTROL (proves the probe is sound, not the finding): sibling table 1_natturufar/2_vedurfar/UMH11130.px, same folder, same date-tail since=2024-12-31 -> GET 200, metadata DOES carry `time: True` on 'Ar'; POST 200, 4456 bytes, response carries `"role":{"time":["Ar"]}`; resolve_time_dim locks on 'Ar' authoritatively and parse_jsonstat2 returns 64 rows -> classified 'data'. Identical request shape, identical publisher, works. The only difference is the presence of the authoritative time flag.
- file:line for the bug: updater/strategies/fetchers/hagstofa.py:356 `tvar = _time_var(variables)` correctly resolves the time axis from the FULL metadata (my probe printed `resolved tvar code = Ar` for both offenders), but line 378 then recomputes `meta_time_code = next((v.get('code') for v in variables if v.get('time') is True), None)` -> None, and line 379 `rows = parse_jsonstat2(resp, prefix, meta_time_code)` passes that None, DISCARDING the axis it just resolved and forcing the parser to re-guess from the truncated response.
- file:line for the misclassification: updater/strategies/fetchers/hagstofa.py:382-386 - `body_has_values = bool(resp.get('value'))`; with since_date set and a non-empty value array this returns 'structural', which reaches _common.finalize() (updater/strategies/fetchers/_common.py:266-269) and raises DefinitiveError for the WHOLE source.
- NOT a budget deferral in the R303 sense, but note the run only attempted 1074 of the 1906 catalog tables (30-min HAGSTOFA_BUDGET_MIN); the fetcher's budget `break` at hagstofa.py never calls tally.deferred_unit(), so the ~832 untouched tables appear nowhere in the tally - the denominator 1074 is honest, the missing 832 are simply silent.

## 6. Rules that apply to every repair here

- **A key/parser change is a RE-PULL, never a merge** (R22). Changing what `series_key` means leaves the old and new grains coexisting; dedup cannot collapse them because they no longer collide. Use `mode="replace"`, or re-pull the table.
- **Never patch dates — re-pull** (R288). A naive date repair on `cso` would have destroyed 11 of 12 rows; only a negative control caught it. And 41,091 of `stat_slovenia`'s fabricated dates land in 1900–2200, indistinguishable from real data, so no date test can find them.
- **Verify against the store you are actually serving** (R296/R36). Under `AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2` the local directory is a scratch mirror of the last run only; a local check can under-report or give the opposite answer.
- **When a probe reports ABSENCE, run it against something known PRESENT** (R316). An absence looks identical whether the data is missing or the probe is broken.
- **Compare (key, date) pairs, not just keys** (R314). A re-key check that compares identifiers verifies the half you changed on purpose; the half you changed by accident is in the values.
- **A bound over a fixed order is a truncation, not a budget** (R190). If work is capped, check it ROTATES — and specifically that it rotates when the item at the head never completes (R313).
- **Read the job's ARGV, not its progress** (R323). A `--dry-run` and a real run print the same numbers.
